stem: Read the clues below carefully and answer: (1) P is the father of Q. (2) R is the son of S. (3) S is the daughter of P. (4) T is the husband of P's daughter. (5) R has no siblings. Who is T's father-in-law?

per_option_rationale.rationale: T is the husband of P's daughter. P is the father of that daughter. Therefore T's father-in-law is P.
Q is P's child (same generation as S). T's father-in-law must be the father of T's wife. Q is not necessarily the father of any of P's daughters mentioned; P is the father.

S is P's daughter, so S is T's wife (since T is the husband of P's daughter and R has no siblings means S has no sisters, making S uniquely T's wife). S is female, so S cannot be a father-in-law; the father-in-law is S's father, which is P.
R is S's son, so R is one generation below T's wife. A son of one's wife is a stepson, not a father-in-law. This confuses a descendant with an ancestor.

explanation: From clue 3, S is P's daughter. From clue 5, R has no siblings, so S has only one child (R). From clue 4, T is the husband of P's daughter. Since S is P's daughter, T's wife is S (the only available daughter of P in the clues). T's father-in-law is S's father, which is P.

explanation_sections.punchline: T is married to P's daughter S, so T's father-in-law is directly P.
explanation_sections.approach: Apply clues most-certain-first: Clue 3 gives S as P's daughter. Clue 4 says T is husband of P's daughter => T's wife is S. Father-in-law = wife's father = P.
explanation_sections.lesson: Father-in-law is the father of one's spouse; trace back from spouse to her father, not sideways or downward.
explanation_sections.timing: About 70 seconds. Trap is option 3 (S), confusing gender: S is female so cannot be 'father-in-law'. Eliminating S immediately leaves P as the correct answer.
